articles.title: Rochdale Council Wins North West Employers Trisector Challenge
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council staff have triumphed in the North West Employers Trisector Challenge, outperforming 13 local authorities to secure a prestigious award.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council staff have achieved recognition by winning the North West Employers Trisector Challenge, surpassing 13 other local authorities in the competition. The event took place at the Halliwell Jones Stadium in Warrington, home of the Warrington Wolves, and aimed to provide aspiring leaders with insights into senior management challenges across various sectors, including local government, police, fire services, NHS, housing associations, and education.

To succeed in the challenge, teams were required to collaborate with neighbouring stakeholders and partners to devise a new strategy for their organisations. Participants had to prioritise key areas, navigate politically sensitive issues, and maintain a focus on customer service while addressing the constraints of limited resources.

Following the announcement of their victory, the Mayor of Rochdale, Councillor Faisal Rana, commended the efforts of the council staff, stating, "Well done to all the staff at Rochdale Borough Council for winning the North West Trisector Challenge!" This accolade not only highlights the dedication of the council staff but also reflects positively on the services provided to the community.

The win may enhance the council's reputation and could lead to further opportunities for collaboration and improvement in public services. As the council continues to navigate challenges, this recognition serves as a testament to their commitment to delivering quality services to the residents of Rochdale.

articles.title: Northern Care Alliance Staff Strike Over Overtime Payments at Rochdale Infirmary
articles.excerpt: Over 350 staff from the Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust are striking over overtime payment disputes, affecting services at Rochdale Infirmary and other hospitals.
articles.content_html:
Hundreds of operating theatre staff from the Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust returned to the picket lines this morning as part of a three-day strike over overtime payments. More than 350 members of the Unison union, employed at Rochdale Infirmary, Salford Royal Hospital, Fairfield General Hospital, and Royal Oldham Hospital, are participating in the industrial action due to disputes regarding overtime compensation.

The strike centres on the issue of time-and-a-half payments that staff are entitled to when covering for staff shortages. Unison claims that the use of agency staff has resulted in some trust employees earning less than they would on a normal shift, with some missing out on over £80 per shift. This has led to significant discontent among the workforce, prompting the current strike action.

In response to the ongoing dispute, hospital management has declared a critical incident, allowing them to bring in additional support to maintain urgent surgical services. However, some procedures are expected to be postponed as theatre staff, including nurses and clinical support workers, join the picket lines. This follows a previous strike in June, which was called off after an agreement appeared to be reached, but Unison stated that the offer was later withdrawn.

Kevin Dolan, a regional organiser for Unison, expressed frustration over the situation, stating that the leadership at the Northern Care Alliance has shown a lack of regard for their staff. The trust has acknowledged the challenges it faces and is working to address concerns while focusing on improving safety and care standards. The outcome of this strike could have significant implications for staffing and patient care at local hospitals.

articles.title: Masdar Launches 35MW Battery Energy Storage System in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Masdar has commenced operations at a new 35MW battery energy storage system in Rochdale, contributing to the UK's renewable energy goals and grid stability.
articles.content_html:
Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC, known as Masdar, has officially begun commercial operations at its 35-megawatt (MW) battery energy storage system (BESS) located in Rochdale, England. This facility, which has a storage capacity of 70 megawatt hours (MWh), is designed to provide clean energy for approximately 35,000 homes daily, marking a significant step in Masdar's commitment to expanding its renewable energy portfolio in the UK.

The Rochdale BESS is part of Masdar's broader strategy to develop a three-gigawatt-hour (GWh) battery storage capacity across the UK, following the company's acquisition of Arlington Energy Ltd in 2022. The total investment earmarked for this initiative is around £1 billion (approximately $1.36 billion). The facility will also play a crucial role in providing grid balancing services, responding to fluctuations in electricity supply and demand within milliseconds, thereby enhancing the reliability of the electricity network.

Masdar's entry into the UK battery storage market follows the successful launch of its first project, a 20 MW/40 MWh BESS in Stockport, which became operational in December 2025. The company is also developing additional projects in Chesterfield and Cardiff, which will collectively add 150 MW/300 MWh to its portfolio. Recently, Masdar secured £97 million in financing for these projects, further solidifying its commitment to renewable energy in the region.

The UK government aims to install 27.1 GWh of battery storage capacity by the end of the decade under its Clean Power 2030 Action Plan. Masdar's initiatives align with this goal, as the company continues to invest in both battery storage and offshore wind projects, including the East Anglia 3 wind project, which is expected to power approximately 1.3 million homes. As demand for electricity rises, driven by electrification and technological advancements, Masdar is positioning itself as a leader in battery storage solutions.

articles.title: Autechre Reflects on Early Music Production Techniques in 1994 Interview
articles.excerpt: In a recent retrospective, Autechre, the influential electronic music duo formed in Rochdale, discussed their initial workflow and the gear they used to create their pioneering sound.
articles.content_html:
Autechre, the renowned electronic music duo formed in Rochdale in 1987, recently reflected on their early music production techniques in an interview originally conducted in 1994. The duo, consisting of Rob Brown and Sean Booth, shared insights into their creative process and the equipment that shaped their influential sound.

During the interview, which took place shortly after the release of their second album, Amber, Booth explained how they would collaborate on music by mixing tracks at Brown's house before moving to his own to edit and refine their work. They drew inspiration from early hip-hop techniques, particularly the pause-button edits popularised by artists like Mantronix.

Autechre's legacy in electronic music is significant, with their innovative approach influencing countless producers over the past three decades. Their discography includes seminal albums such as 1993's Incunabula and 1995's Tri Repetae, which are often cited as pivotal works in the genre of Intelligent Dance Music (IDM).

As Autechre continues to evolve their sound, their commitment to understanding and mastering new technology remains a cornerstone of their artistic philosophy. This dedication not only highlights their growth as artists but also serves as an inspiration for emerging musicians in the electronic music scene. Their journey from humble beginnings in Rochdale to becoming icons in the music industry exemplifies the impact of local talent on the global stage.

articles.title: £40 Million Partnership to Deliver 158 Affordable Homes at Trub Farm, Castleton
articles.excerpt: A new partnership between L&G Affordable Homes and MCI Developments will create 158 affordable homes in Castleton, Rochdale, as part of a £40 million scheme approved by the council.
articles.content_html:
A partnership between L&G Affordable Homes and MCI Developments will deliver 158 affordable homes in a £40 million scheme at Trub Farm, Castleton, Rochdale. The project received full planning permission from Rochdale Borough Council last month and will feature a mix of one- and two-bedroom apartments, as well as two-, three-, and four-bedroom houses.

L&G Affordable Homes will manage the properties, offering them as social rent and shared ownership. Jamie Irving, land and partnerships director at MCI Developments, expressed pride in the collaboration, stating that it reflects a commitment to providing high-quality homes where they are needed most. He added that the scheme aims to support the creation of a thriving community in Rochdale.

The development will also include a cycle and pedestrian path that connects the neighbourhood to the adjacent Rochdale Canal towpath, enhancing accessibility for residents. Marcus Fisher, head of new business at L&G Affordable Homes, highlighted the importance of this scheme for the area, noting that partnerships like this are crucial for delivering long-term stability and investment in housing projects.

Construction is set to begin soon, with further details on timelines and completion dates expected to be announced in the coming months. This initiative is part of ongoing efforts to address the demand for affordable housing in Rochdale, contributing to the local community's growth and development.
